'''Akita Suwa Shrine''' (秋田諏訪宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in [[Misato Town]], {{ill|Senboku District|eo|Distrikto Semboku|fr|District de Senboku|it|Distretto di Senboku|ko|센보쿠군|qid=Q398444|lt=Senboku District}}, {{ill|Akita Prefecture|en|Akita Prefecture|qid=Q81863|lt=Akita Prefecture}}. The shrine was formerly Ranked as a prefectural shrine and is currently listed as a Beppyo Shrine under the jurisdiction of the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]].

During the [[:en:Later Three-Year War|Later Three-Year War]], it is said that Suwa Daimyojin from {{ill|Shinano Province|ckb|پارێزگای شینانۆ|cs|Provincie Šinano|de|Provinz Shinano|eo|Provinco Ŝinano|es|Provincia de Shinano|fa|ولایت شینانو|fr|Province de Shinano|gl|Provincia de Shinano|hak|Shinano-koet|id|Provinsi Shinano|it|Shinano (provincia)|ja|信濃国|knc|Shinano Province|ko|시나노국|lt|Šinano žemė|ms|Wilayah Shinano|nl|Shinano (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Shinano|pt|Província de Shinano|ru|Синано (провинция)|simple|Shinano Province|sk|Šinano (provincia)|sr|Провинција Шинано|th|แคว้นชินาโนะ|tr|Shinano (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Сінано|zh|信濃國|zh_min_nan|Sinano-kok|zh_yue|信濃國|qid=Q289250|lt=Shinano Province}} worshiped at the shrine while in camp. Upon his return, he enshrined a statue of a Daiguji (chief priest) and left one son to serve as a priest, establishing the Suwa (Suwa) family as hereditary chief priests.

* {{ill|1810|en|1810|qid=Q6922|lt=1810}} (Bunka 7) - "Suwa Shrine" plaque inscribed by Yokote Castle governor Tomura Yoshimichi installed.
* {{ill|1845|en|1845|qid=Q7636|lt=1845}} (Kōka 2) - The chief priest became directly controlled by the Jisha-bugyō (temple and shrine magistrate).
* {{ill|1869|en|1869|qid=Q7720|lt=1869}} (Meiji 2) - The shrine was designated as the general protector of {{ill|Ugo Province|en|Ugo Province|qid=Q1192070|lt=Ugo Province}}.
* {{ill|1881|en|1881|qid=Q7808|lt=1881}} (Meiji 14) - The shrine served as a rest stop during the {{ill|Emperor Meiji|en|Emperor Meiji|qid=Q174231|lt=Emperor Meiji}}'s tour of the Tohoku region<ref name="akitajiten"/>.
* {{ill|1919|en|1919|qid=Q2157|lt=1919}} (Taisho 8) - Ranked as a prefectural shrine.
* {{ill|1920|en|1920|qid=Q2155|lt=1920}} (Taisho 9) - Current worship hall built.
* {{ill|1953|en|1953|qid=Q18585|lt=1953}} (Showa 28) - Listed as a Beppyo Shrine.
* {{ill|1987|en|1987|qid=Q2429|lt=1987}} (Showa 62) - Officially named Akita Suwa Shrine.
The shrine is unique in Akita Prefecture for having maintained its status as an independent Shinto shrine, without becoming associated with Buddhist or Shugendo temples, even before the Kami-Buddha Separation Order. The Suwa family has consistently held the Rank of Shinto priest.
The shrine is known for the unique [[:en:Koshogatsu|Koshogatsu]] ritual "Rokugo Kamakura festival," which includes the "Takeuchi" (Bamboo Battle) ceremony, designated as a [[National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property]] on January 14, 1982.
== Deities ==
The shrine enshrines [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata no Mikoto]], [[Yasakatome no Mikoto]], among others.

== Access ==
* By bus: 20 minutes from {{ill|JR|en|JR|qid=Q127942|lt=JR}} {{ill|Ōmagari Station (Akita)|en|Ōmagari Station (Akita)|qid=Q1052987|lt=Ōmagari Station}} on [[Ugo Kotsu]] Bus, get off at Rokugo-Ōmachi or Rokugo-Kamimachi Bus Stop, then 5-minute walk.
* By taxi: 5 minutes from {{ill|JR|en|JR|qid=Q127942|lt=JR}} {{ill|Iizume Station|en|Iizume Station|qid=Q5995055|lt=Iizume Station}} (3.5 km).
* By car: 30 minutes from [[Yokote Interchange]] on the {{ill|Akita Expressway|en|Akita Expressway|qid=Q1060262|lt=Akita Expressway}} (17 km), 20 minutes from [[Ōmagari Interchange]] (12 km).
